sites.evidence_type: published tag insertion in the same loop or domain
sites.functional_impact_measured: Protein detected by anti-Myc antibody in an in vitro transcription/translation system; cell-surface trafficking and receptor-binding function NOT MEASURED.
sites.rationale: Zebra finch ephrin-B3 residue 21 is the first residue of the mature ectodomain in that ortholog (signal peptide ~20 aa); the equivalent junction in human EFNB3 is after residue 27, the last residue of the human signal peptide (landmarks: SP 1–27, extracellular 28–227). Python confirms residue 27 = G and residue 28 = L. The junction is 200 residues from the TM boundary (TM starts at 228), satisfying the ≥3-residue rule. Position_evidence is topology_derived because the cited residue belongs to the ortholog and the human junction is recovered from the SP cleavage landmark, not from a human-specific experiment. L1 reports a full-length, membrane-anchored zebra finch ephrin-B3 construct in which four myc epitope repeats were inserted between an Ig κ chain signal sequence and predicted residue 21 of zebra finch ephrin-B3 (the first residue of the mature ectodomain in that ortholog), for detection of in vitro transcribed protein.

sources.claim: For detection of the in vitro transcribed protein, four repeats of the myc epitope were inserted between the Ig κ chain signal sequence and predicted residue 21 of zebra finch ephrin-B3.

literature_notes: Only one ledger line (L1) was provided. It reports a full-length, membrane-anchored zebra finch ephrin-B3 construct with a 4x Myc tag placed at the N-terminus of the mature ectodomain (after the signal peptide), validated only in an in vitro transcription/translation system. Because the source is an ortholog and the validation is minimal (no cell-surface expression assay, no functional assay), confidence is low. No ledger evidence supports any internal extracellular loop site or the C-terminal (intracellular) terminus of human EFNB3. The large extracellular domain (residues 28–227) contains the EphB-receptor-binding surface; an N-terminal tag may interfere with receptor engagement, but this was not tested in L1.
